title: enhance-openai-compat-layer-with-requestid-trace-and-route-metrics-tags
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Several customers and internal dashboards showed gaps in API-surface observability for OpenAI-compat traffic: request IDs were not reliably present in streaming responses, trace context could be lost during async batching and tool/function-calling handoffs, and metrics were not tagged per-route/model which made cost and latency debugging difficult. This PR instruments the API surface and the OpenAI compatibility adapter to provide deterministic request IDs, propagate trace context through streaming frames and tool-calls, emit structured JSON logs with route and model tags, and attach per-endpoint metrics tags.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a request-id middleware that generates a UUIDv4 when missing, sets X-Request-Id on the response, and injects request_id into the request context and structured logger.
- Ensures trace propagation: extracts traceparent (W3C) and stores it alongside request_id; the trace id is forwarded to downstream internal calls and included in streaming meta frames.
- Updates streaming runtime to emit an initial metadata chunk for streaming responses. The chunk is a small JSON meta frame that includes request_id and trace (and route/model tags). Example streaming meta chunk (first frame): {"meta":{"request_id":"<uuid>","trace":"00-<traceid>-<spanid>-01","route":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"gpt-redwood-1","compat":"openai"}}
- Changes OpenAI-compat adapter to copy X-Request-Id to proxied upstream requests (and accept request-id from upstream), and to include request_id in function/tool-calling result envelopes so observability correlates generated tool output with original API request.
- Adds per-route and per-model metric tags (route, model, compat, streaming) at the instrumentation layer so metrics (latency, tokens, errors) are sliceable in dashboards and cost reports.
- Switches API logging to structured JSON for request/response lifecycle events emitted by middleware and the adapter (log keys: ts, level, request_id, trace, route, op, latency_ms, status, model, client_id_hash).
- Adds unit and e2e tests for middleware, streaming meta frame emission, OpenAI-compat header propagation, and a small integration test that verifies metric tags are present in exported dogstatsd/prom lines.
- Documentation: concise observability guide for OpenAI-compat consumers and operators (docs/observability/openai-compat.md) describing the new meta frame format and example Prometheus/dash queries.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Streaming meta frames are emitted as the first chunk in all streaming responses. We opted for a small single-frame JSON meta envelope to avoid changing the tokenization or user-visible text. The meta frame is optional for non-streaming responses.
- To keep backward compatibility with older clients we emit the meta frame only when the client sets Accept: application/json or the compatibility adapter detects openai-streaming semantics; otherwise the meta header X-Request-Id is always present in non-streaming responses.
- We avoided adding a new HTTP header per metric tag (would be expensive at edge) and instead tag metrics server-side using the route name and model extracted from the request payload.
- Security: request_id is opaque and not PII. client_id is hashed before logging.

Rollout plan:
- Step 1: Deploy middleware and metrics tagging to staging, run e2e streaming tests and verify dashboards (currently done in staging).
- Step 2: Merge and deploy to canary hosts (10% of traffic) for 24h, monitor error rates, latency and token cost splits.
- Step 3: Full rollout once canary metrics are normal.

Backward compatibility: Non-streaming clients see only the X-Request-Id header (unchanged semantics). Streaming clients that do not expect the meta frame will still receive tokens; we documented the meta envelope and guard emission by compat detection.

Checklist:
- [x] request-id middleware + unit tests
- [x] streaming runtime changes + e2e tests
- [x] openai-compat adapter header propagation and tool-call envelope updates
- [x] structured logging and metric tags
- [x] docs and example queries
- [x] CI green after a follow-up fix for a flaky stream test

Why this is safe: Changes are additive and do not alter normal token payloads except for the initial meta chunk in streaming responses (conditioned by compat header). Observability improvements are read-only for user content and do not modify downstream model I/O beyond headers and envelope metadata.

review_comments: Leah Gomez: Small nit in request_id middleware: prefer uuid.NewRandom() vs time-based generation; otherwise looks good.
Arjun Patel: Can we avoid attaching the meta frame for legacy clients? Suggest adding a header Accept: application/vnd.openai+json; implemented a guard.
Jonah Weiss: We should include model tag earlier (before batching) so router metrics can aggregate correctly; updated metrics/tags.go to capture model at parse time.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed Leah and Arjun comments; added guard for legacy clients and switched UUID generation. Jonah's model-tagting changes are included and tests added.
Leah Gomez (approve): Tests look rigorous; approve pending CI green.

release_notes: Added request-id propagation and trace metadata for OpenAI-compat streaming responses; structured JSON logs now include request_id, trace, route and model; metrics are tagged per-route/model to improve observability and cost attribution.
